summary: Feed s163_triple is degraded for IDS: 38.3% one-way TCP sessions, 5.1% TCP packet drops, and 7.5% duplicates. IDS requires both directions and full payload - missing directions and gaps prevent stream reassembly and signature matching.

findings.root_cause: Only one direction of TCP sessions is reaching the IDS (59/154 sessions one-way, 38.3%). Most likely asymmetric routing with separate SPAN/monitor sessions not aggregated, or packet broker policy forwarding only one side of the flow to this tool port.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS needs both directions to reassemble TCP streams and correlate request/response. One-way traffic causes missed detections, broken state tracking, and high false negatives for IDS signatures.

recommended_fix.why: Aggregate both directions of each flow to the same IDS tool port so bidirectional sessions are complete for reassembly.

findings.root_cause: 5.1% of TCP packets show gaps/retransmissions indicating missing data (100/1957). With tool not overloaded, drops are upstream - typically SPAN oversubscription/truncation or packet broker buffer drops under burst.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS requires full payload; gaps prevent payload inspection, file extraction and signature matching, allowing evasions and missed exploits.

recommended_fix.why: Replace lossy SPAN with passive TAP and ensure broker has sufficient buffering/bandwidth to deliver lossless, complete packets to the 1Gbps IDS port.

findings.root_cause: 7.5% duplicate packets (152/2036) indicates overlapping SPAN sources or dual-sided TAP aggregation without deduplication at the packet broker.
findings.impact_on_tool: Duplicates waste IDS processing capacity on 1Gbps port, inflate session counts, distort analytics and can cause false positives or signature misfires.

recommended_fix.why: Enable broker-level deduplication to strip duplicates before delivery while preserving one complete copy of each packet.
